                         REGULAR MEETING OF THE COUNCIL

                                           OF THE

                                  CITY OF BIRMINGHAM

                           FEBRUA RY 17, 20 26 at 9:00 A.M.

      The Council of the City of Birmingham met in the Council Chambers of the City Hall of
Birmingham on February 24, 2026, at 9:30 a.m., in regular meeting.

       The meeting was opened with prayer by Reverend James Bell, Associate Minister, New
Pilgrim Baptist Church of Birmingham, AL.

       The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilor Hunter Williams.

       Present on Roll Call:       Council President    Alexander
                                   Councilmembers       Gunn
                                                        O’Quinn
                                                        Smith
                                                        Smitherman
                                                        Tate
                                                        Vasa
                                                        Williams (Arrived as herein indicated)
                                                        Woods


       Mayor Randall Woodfin honored the life of George Barber.


      The following resolutions and ordinances designated as Consent Agenda items were
introduced by the Presiding Officer:


                                  RESOLUTION NO. 413-26

       BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham, that the application
submitted by Tulip BHM Hospitality, LLC to the City of Birmingham, Alabama, dated January 14,
2026, for the transfer of a Restaurant Retail Liquor License to be used at 5000 Richard Arrington
Jr. Boulevard. North, Birmingham, Alabama 35212, be and the same hereby is approved and
recommended for grant by the Alabama Alcoholic Beverage Control Board, provided that this
recommendation for grant of such license is hereby conditioned upon said applicant having or
obtaining a certificate of occupancy from the Director of Planning, Engineering, and Permits for
said premises no later than ninety days from the date of this action.
                                           FEB 17 2026                                         3

                                   RESOLUTION NO. 414-26

        WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 8/22/2023, by Resolution No. 1395-23 the Council of the City
of Birmingham, at its regularly scheduled meetings declared the properties described below to be a
public nuisance

        WHEREAS, all proper notices were posted and delivered by certified mail to the persons,
firms, associations or corporations last assessing the below described properties for state taxes as
required by Act No. 105 of the Third Special Session of the Alabama Legislature, 1971 and as
amended by Act 91-192; and

       WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 9/26/2023, Resolution No. 1617-23 by the Council of the City of
Birmingham, having heard all protests or objections presented, declared the noxious or dangerous
weeds on said properties to be a public and nuisance and directed that said nuisance be abated by
the removal of said weeds by the City; and

        WHEREAS, said weeds have been cleared from the properties described below and the
cost of such clearing has been reported to the council; and

       WHEREAS, notice has been given as required by law that on this date and time the
Council would consider a resolution fixing the costs and assessing said costs against the properties
described herein;

        NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham
that:

1.      It is hereby ascertained by the Council that the below sums were reasonably incurred as the
cost of clearing the herein below described premises.

2.     The below sums shall be hereby fixed as a special assessment against the properties
hereinafter described and that such sums shall constitute a lien upon said properties for the amount
of such assessments and shall continue in force until paid.

3.      The name of the persons, firm, association or corporation last assessing the said properties
for state taxes, a description of the properties assessed for said costs and the amount of such
assessments for said costs is hereby determined, adjudged and fixed as follows, to-wit:

                                      RESOLUTION NO. 418-26

        WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 9/17/2024, by Resolution No. 1471-24 the Council of the City
of Birmingham, at its regularly scheduled meetings declared the properties described below to be a
public nuisance

        WHEREAS, all proper notices were posted and delivered by certified mail to the persons,
firms, associations or corporations last assessing the below described properties for state taxes as
required by Act No. 105 of the Third Special Session of the Alabama Legislature, 1971 and as
amended by Act 91-192; and

       WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 10/22/2024, Resolution No. 1617-24 by the Council of the City
of Birmingham, having heard all protests or objections presented, declared the noxious or
dangerous weeds on said properties to be a public and nuisance and directed that said nuisance be
abated by the removal of said weeds by the City; and

        WHEREAS, said weeds have been cleared from the properties described below and the
cost of such clearing has been reported to the council; and
                                            FEB 17 2026                                       16



       WHEREAS, notice has been given as required by law that on this date and time the
Council would consider a resolution fixing the costs and assessing said costs against the properties
described herein;

        NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham
that:

1.      It is hereby ascertained by the Council that the below sums were reasonably incurred as the
cost of clearing the herein below described premises.

2.     The below sums shall be hereby fixed as a special assessment against the properties
hereinafter described and that such sums shall constitute a lien upon said properties for the amount
of such assessments and shall continue in force until paid.


3.      The name of the persons, firm, association or corporation last assessing the said properties
for state taxes, a description of the properties assessed for said costs and the amount of such
assessments for said costs is hereby determined, adjudged and fixed as follows, to-wit:

                                        RESOLUTION NO. 419-26

       WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 10/3/2023, by Resolution No. 1660-23 the Council of the City of
Birmingham, at its regularly scheduled meetings declared the properties described below to be a
public nuisance

       WHEREAS, all proper notices were posted and delivered by certified mail to the persons,
firms, associations or corporations last assessing the below described properties for state taxes as
required by Act No. 105 of the Third Special Session of the Alabama Legislature, 1971 and as
amended by Act 91-192; and

       WHEREAS, on Tuesday, 11/07/2023, Resolution No. 1837-23 by the Council of the City
of Birmingham, having heard all protests or objections presented, declared the noxious or
dangerous weeds on said properties to be a public and nuisance and directed that said nuisance be
abated by the removal of said weeds by the City; and

        WHEREAS, said weeds have been cleared from the properties described below and the
cost of such clearing has been reported to the council; and

       WHEREAS, notice has been given as required by law that on this date and time the
Council would consider a resolution fixing the costs and assessing said costs against the properties
described herein;

        NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham
that:

1.      It is hereby ascertained by the Council that the below sums were reasonably incurred as the
cost of clearing the herein below described premises.
                                           FEB 17 2026                                        26



2.     The below sums shall be hereby fixed as a special assessment against the properties
hereinafter described and that such sums shall constitute a lien upon said properties for the amount
of such assessments and shall continue in force until paid.

for state taxes, a description of the properties assessed for said costs and the amount of such
assessments for said costs is hereby determined, adjudged and fixed as follows, to-wit:

                                 RESOLUTION NO. 422-26

       BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham that Resolution No. 2220-
25 adopted by the Council on December 9, 2025 which assessed properties throughout the City for
the abatement of noxious or dangerous weeds, be and hereby is amended to remove the following

       The following resolution was introduced by Councilmember Williams:

                                   Case No. SUB 2025-00064

                                  RESOLUTION NO. 430-26

       WHEREAS, there has been exhibited to this Council a duly acknowledged Declaration of

Vacation executed River Brook Realty, being the owners, and the reading in part as follows:

       KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENT, that the undersigned, River Brook Realty,
owners of all lands abutting the portion of public way or ways hereinafter declared vacated, does
hereby declare vacated and divested out of the public the portion or portions of public way or ways
described as follows, to-wit:
                                        Legal Description

A Boundary Survey of a part of the following situated in the North 1/2 of the Northeast 1/4 of
Section 13, Township 17 South, Range 13 West, Jefferson County, Alabama. Lots 1 thru 3, Block
                                            FEB 17 2026                                         41

3, Less and Except the N.W. 50 feet and all of Lots 20 thru 24, Block 3 and Lot 6-A, Block 3, and
Lot 6-A, Resurvey of Lots 4-A and 5-A, including the vacated 34th Street North, Fairfield
according to a Resurvey Blocks 4 and 5, Fairfield, as recorded in Map Book 128, page 82, in the
Office of the Judge of Probate in Jefferson County, Alabama, and Lot 6-A, Block 3 of the
Resurvey Of Lots 4-A & 5-A including The Vacated 34th Street North, Fairfield according to A
Resurvey of Block 4 & 5, Fairfield North Birmingham Realty Company's Addition to North
Birmingham as Recorded in Map Book 113, Page 10.

PARCEL A: Lots 1 thru 3, Block 3, except the N.W. 50 feet and all Lots 20 thru 24 Blk 3 Fairfield
Addition to North Birmingham, also that part of vacated 33rd Place North & vacated alley
description as recorded in Map Book 7, Page 2 and is more particularly described as follows:
Begin at S.W. corner of said Lot 3; thence S.W. 10 feet; thence S.E. 253.3 feet; thence East 220
feet; thence N.W. 422.2 feet; thence S.W. 200 feet; thence S.E. 90 feet to point of beginning.

PARCEL B: Lot 6-A, Resurvey of lots 4-A and 5-A, including the vacated 34th street north,
Fairfield according to a Resurvey Blocks 4 and 5, Fairfield, as recorded in map book 128, page 82,
in the Office of the Judge of Probate in Jefferson County, Alabama.


**Right-of-Way to be Vacated:**

1. **10’ Alley Right-of-Way (Unnamed):**
A 10-foot-wide public alley located in Block 3 of the Fairfield Addition to North Birmingham
(Map Book 7, Page 2), lying between Lots 1–3 and 20–24, to be vacated and incorporated into
adjacent parcels.

2. **50’ Street Right-of-Way (Former 33rd Place North / 34th Street North):**
A 50-foot-wide street right-of-way running between the Resurvey of Lots 4-A and 5-A and Lot 6-
A, as recorded in Map Book 128, Page 82 and Map Book 113, Page 10. Said right-of-way lies
entirely within the corporate limits of the City of Birmingham and is shown on the final plat
prepared by Trademark Engineering.

**Total Right-of-Way Area to be Vacated: 24,658.27 square feet**

       The vacation hereinabove declared shall be subject to such conditions and reservations for
the benefit of the owners or operators of public utilities or installations in said way or ways as the
governing body of the City of Birmingham may see fit to specify in a resolution of assent.
                                            FEB 17 2026                                          42

       The said owner does further declare that after the vacation hereinabove declared,
convenient means of ingress and egress to and from their respective properties will be afforded to
all other property owners by the remaining public ways dedicated to the public for public way
purposes, and,

        WHEREAS, it has been made to appear to this Council that said declarant is the owner of
all the land abutting on the portion or portions of public way or ways declared vacated by said
Declaration of Vacation and that after the vacation of the said portion or portions of said public
way or ways convenient means of ingress and egress to and from their property will be afforded to
all other property owners by the remaining public grounds dedicated to the public for public way
purposes; and

       NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham as
follows:

       1.      After hearing all parties and considering all information presented, the assent of this
Council be, and hereby is given and granted to the vacation of the portion, or portions, of public
way or ways declared vacated in the above quoted Declaration of Vacation, subject to the
conditions and reservations hereinafter set out, and further, this Council finds that all other
property owners will have convenient means of ingress and egress to and from their property by
the remaining public grounds dedicated to the public for public way purposes and that it is in the
best interest of the public that the above described public way or ways or portions thereof be
vacated.

        2.      That the foregoing assent be and is hereby given upon condition that any entity,
including the City of Birmingham, which may now own or rightfully maintain any public utility,
facility, line or installation, including any open or closed storm or sanitary sewer, in any portion of
any public way hereinabove mentioned, shall have a right and easement to continue to maintain
same in its present location therein and to repair, cleanse, improve and reconstruct the same and to
have convenient storm water drainage and sanitary sewer means thereto and there from for said
purposes, and that there be and is hereby reserved and excluded from the said foregoing assent any
assent of this Council to the vacation, annulment or impairment of the right, easement or privilege
of any such entity to continue to own, maintain, repair, cleanse, improve, reconstruct and have
convenient means of ingress and egress to and from such utility, facility, line or installation.

        3.      The foregoing provisions for maintenance and for ingress and egress shall mean,
among other things and without limitation, that in case any building or edifice shall be constructed
or placed in any portion of any of said vacated ways, it shall be constructed, placed or arranged
therein so as to avoid damage to any presently existing concealed or unconcealed or patent or
latent public utility, facility, line or installation in any such public way and so as to afford ways
and means of ingress and egress to and from such utility, facility, line or installation for purpose of
reconstruction, repair, cleansing or improvement of service of same, substantially equal to and as
convenient as presently existing ways and means of ingress and egress thereto and therefrom such
purposes, or such as shall be approved in writing by the owner or operator of such utility, facility,
line or installation.
                                          FEB 17 2026                                        43



       4.      This resolution shall be effective only upon the payment of the right-of-way fee
within sixty (60) days of the date of this resolution, the recording in the Office of the Judge of
Probate of Jefferson County, Alabama, of a map or plat approved by the City Engineer and the
Birmingham Planning Commission showing the vacated portion or portions of public way or ways
as described above and the boundary lines of the abutting property resulting from the vacation, and
notice of the governing body’s action being published once in a newspaper in the county no later
than 14 days after its adoption.

        The resolution was read by the City Clerk, whereupon Councilmember Williams moved its
adoption which motion was seconded by Councilmember Smitherman, and upon the roll being
called the vote was as follows:

       Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Williams, Woods, Tate, Alexander
       Nays: None

       The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
the resolution adopted.


       The following ordinance was introduced by Councilmember Williams:

                                    ORDINANCE NO. 26-12

          TO AUTHORIZE THE CHIEF OF POLICE TO EXECUTE A
       CONTRACTOR/VENDOR CJI ACCESS SECURITY AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN THE ALABAMA LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY, ALABAMA POWER
               COMPANY AND THE CITY OF BIRMINGHAM

        WHEREAS, the ALABAMA LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY (“ALEA”),
ALABAMA POWER COMPANY (‘APC”), an electric public utility, and the CITY OF
BIRMINGHAM, a municipal corporation, (hereinafter referred to as “City” or “BPD”) desire to
enter into a Contractor/Vendor CJI Access Security Agreement for a term of up to three years, to
verify that Alabama Power has a specific agreement with the City of Birmingham (for BPD) to
provide specific CJI sharing services and/or products for the administration of justice; and

      WHEREAS, Section 41-9-591(a), Code of Alabama, authorizes ALEA to administer the
Alabama Justice Information Commission’s policies and procedures and to operate ALEA CJS
information systems for the purpose of accessing, accumulating, storing, retrieving, analyzing, and
disseminating criminal information; and

       WHEREAS, Act 1969-916 of the Acts of Alabama authorizes Jefferson County and the
municipalities, other governmental subdivisions and public corporations in Jefferson County to
make the most efficient use of their powers by enabling them to cooperate with the state, the
federal government and with each other on a basis of mutual advantage and thereby to provide
                                         FEB 17 2026                                      44

services and facilities in a manner and pursuant to forms of governmental organization that will
accord best with geographic, economic, population and other factors influencing the needs and
developments of the county and municipalities and other governmental units and agencies therein;
and

       WHEREAS, the City and APC entered into a Master Contract for Public Safety Services
(Surveillance Equipment – Governmental) dated May 23, 2024 (the “2024 Agreement”) with
subsequent amendments being executed;

      NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City Council of the City of
Birmingham, Alabama as follows:

SECTION 1. Authorization

The Chief of Police for the City of Birmingham, Alabama, pursuant to §41-9-590, et seq., Code of
Alabama and Alabama Act 1969-916, is hereby authorized to execute a Contractor/Vendor CJI
Access Security Agreement for a term of up to three years, between the Alabama Law
Enforcement Agency (ALEA), Alabama Power Company (“APC”), and the City of
Birmingham wherein the Chief of Police will verify that APC has a separate specific agreement
with the City of Birmingham (for BPD) to provide specific CJI sharing services and/or products
for the administration of justice. This agreement involves no costs to the City.

SECTION 2. This Ordinance shall become effective upon approval and publication, or as
otherwise required by law.

      The ordinance was read by the City Clerk, whereupon Councilmember Williams made a
motion that unanimous consent be granted to adopt said ordinance, which motion was seconded by
Councilmember Smitherman, and upon the roll being called, the vote was as follows:

      Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Williams, Woods, Tate, Alexander
      Nays: None

      The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
the motion to give unanimous consent for adoption of said ordinance adopted.

        Whereupon Councilmember Williams made a motion that said ordinance be adopted, which
motion was seconded by Councilmember Smitherman, and upon the roll being called, the vote was
as follows:

      Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Williams, Woods, Tate, Alexander
      Nays: None

       The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
said ordinance adopted.
                                           FEB 17 2026                                      45

       The following resolution was introduced by Councilmember O’Quinn:

                                    RESOLUTION NO. 431-26

             RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THINGS OF VALUE IN AID OF
                       2026 TRAINING AND EDUCATION

      WHEREAS, the City has the inherent authority to provide training for its officers,
employees, and neighborhood volunteers; and

       WHEREAS, the Birmingham City Council wishes to provide training for Neighborhood
Officers, Neighborhood Association Committee Members or Neighborhood Volunteers to attend
                                          FEB 17 2026                                        46

one of three conferences, including either the 2026 Neighborhoods USA (NUSA) Virtual
Conference May 28, 2026 to May 29, 2026, with expenses only including registration in an
amount not to exceed $125 per attendee and not to exceed one (1) attendee per community, or in
the alternative, the 2026 Main Street Now Conference in Tulsa, Oklahoma from April 13, 2026 to
April 15, 2026 with expenses including registration in an amount not to exceed $2,500 per attendee
and not to exceed one (1) attendee per neighborhood, or in the alternative, the Reclaiming Vacant
Properties Conference in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania from September 22, 2026 to September 25,
2026, with expenses including registration in an amount not to exceed $2,500 per attendee and not
to exceed one (1) attendee per community. Registration and expenses shall also include up to ten
(10) Community Resource Services ("CRS") staff members for each conference attended.
Attendees representing neighborhood associations cannot attend more than one (1) conference in a
calendar year; and

WHEREAS, the events, are expected to have several hundred other attendees from other Cities
and Counties in the United States in attendance as well, will serve to educate and train the City's
Neighborhood Officers and employees with a focus of understanding communities and provide
information that will benefit those seeking resources for community and economic development
within the City of Birmingham, Alabama (the "Services").

      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
OF BIRMINGHAM, ALABAMA, as follows:

1.     The recitals set forth above are incorporated herein as the findings of the Council by this
reference.

2.     The mayor is hereby authorized and empowered to execute various agreements with
various vendors for the cost of registration and expenses for Neighborhood Officers,
Neighborhood Association Committee Members or Neighborhood Volunteers to attend one of
three conferences, including either the 2026 Neighborhoods USA (NUSA) Virtual Conference
May 28, 2026 to May 29, 2026, with expenses only including registration in an amount not to
exceed $125 per attendee and not to exceed one (1) attendee per community, or in the alternative,
the 2026 Main Street Now Conference in Tulsa, Oklahoma from April 13, 2026 to April 15, 2026
with expenses including registration in an amount not to exceed $2,500 per attendee and not to
exceed one (1) attendee per neighborhood, or in the alternative, the Reclaiming Vacant Properties
Conference in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania from September 22, 2026 to September 25, 2026, with
expenses including registration in an amount not to exceed $2,500 per attendee and not to exceed
one (1) attendee per community. Attendees representing neighborhood associations cannot attend
more than one (1) conference in a calendar year. Registration and expenses shall also include up to
ten (10) Community Resource Services ("CRS") staff members for each conference attended. The
events will serve to educate and train the Neighborhood Officers and CRRs on a vision of
communities and provide information that will benefit those seeking resources for community and
economic development within the City of Birmingham, Alabama. Said funds to come from the
respective Neighborhood Association funds.
                                            FEB 17 2026                                          47

3.     The expenditure of public funds for the purpose specified will serve a valid and sufficient
public purpose, notwithstanding any incidental benefit accruing to any private entity or entities.

4.      That in case any one or more of the provisions contained in this Resolution shall be held
invalid, illegal, or unenforceable for any reason, the invalidity, illegality or unenforceability shall
not affect any other provision hereof and this Resolution shall be construed as if such invalid,
illegal or unenforceable provision had never been contained herein.

       The resolution was read by the City Clerk, whereupon Councilmember O’Quinn moved its
adoption which motion was seconded by Councilmember Smith, and upon the roll being called the
vote was as follows:

       Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Woods, Tate, Alexander
       Nays: Williams

       The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
the resolution adopted.


       Councilmember Woods absented himself and did not return to the meeting.

Probate of Jefferson County, Alabama, of a map or plat approved by the City Engineer and the
Birmingham Planning Commission showing the vacated portion or portions of public way or ways
as described above and the boundary lines of the abutting property resulting from the vacation, and
                                           FEB 17 2026                                      50

notice of the governing body’s action being published once in a newspaper in the county no later
than 14 days after its adoption.

        The resolution was read by the City Clerk, whereupon Councilmember Williams moved its
adoption which motion was seconded by Councilmember Smitherman, and upon the roll being
called the vote was as follows:

       Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Tate, Alexander
       Nays: Williams

       The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
the resolution adopted.


       The following resolution was introduced by Councilmember Smith:

                                   RESOLUTION NO. 433-26

       BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham, Alabama that Bruce N.
Hooper is hereby nominated to serve as a member of the Birmingham Park and Recreation Board
replacing Scottie Y. McClaney for a term expiring October 8, 2028, and

      BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Birmingham, Alabama that
Michael D. Moore is hereby nominated to serve as a member of the Birmingham Park and
Recreation Board replacing Patrick Talley for a term expiring October 8, 2029, and

       BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that the above nominations be and hereby are confirmed
pursuant to Act No. 529 of the Regular Session of the State Legislature in 1923, Title 62, Section
721-729, Code of Alabama, 1940 and Section 6 as amended by Act No. 87-788, Act No. 88-948
and Act No. 07-310.
       The resolution was read by the City Clerk, whereupon Councilmember Smith moved its
adoption which motion was seconded by Councilmember O’Quinn, and upon the roll being called
the vote was as follows:

       Ayes: Gunn, O’Quinn, Smith, Smitherman, Vasa, Williams, Tate, Alexander
       Nays: None

       The vote was then announced by the City Clerk, whereupon the Presiding Officer declared
the resolution adopted.


     Sherman Sterling, 2413 Reed Road, spoke relative to the Jamaica Strong Disaster Relief
Campaign.
